steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Spray a cookie sheet generously with non-stick cooking spray.
Trim crusts from bread and roll the slices flat.
In a small bowl combine sugar and cinnamon to make a mixture.

In a large mixing bowl, mix softened cream cheese, milk and vanilla until smooth. Spread this mixture onto each slice of flattened bread. Roll each bread slice up. Dip bread/cream cheese rolls in melted butter, roll the blintzes immediately in the sugar-cinnamon mixture. Cut rolls into 1 inch pieces. Arrange the blintzes on the prepared cookie sheet.
Bake for 10 minutes. Serve with sour cream.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheese Blintzes
raw_recipe.description: A modern and speedy take on a traditional old country favorite: These no-fry blintzes have a white-bread base; sugar butter and cream cheese sweeten things up.
raw_recipe.name: Cheese Blintzes

review.reviewBody:
YUM! Just a few things though...

1.) If you are going to cut them up, do it BEFORE you dip them into the melted butter. It makes for a LOT less mess. Personally, I think they are prettier left whole (especially if you are planning on serving them to guests) 2.) I had extras of almost every ingredient except the cinnamon/sugar. My suggestion would be: double the cinnamon, TRIPLE the sugar, and cut all of the rest of the ingredients in half (unless you want to make a TON!). 3.) When you roll the bread slices flat, make sure it is very smashed. Otherwise the butter soaks into the bread too much and makes it really soggy. And last... 4.) Bake them longer than it calls for (about 15 minutes).

I had never had these before, but this recipe is a keeper. I think it would be great to serve at a brunch.

Sinfully good! I only used (1) 8 ounce package of cream cheese....I added a couple tablespoons of confectioner's sugar as suggested by one reader. And I also added a little vanilla along with the milk. I decided to add a couple tablespoons of strawberry jam to the mixture and I was pleased with the results. However, the next time, I will omit the milk as it was a little thin. Instead of dipping the rolls into butter, I sprayed them with Parkay spray margarine and then dusted them with cinnamon sugar. This will be a regular on my "sweets" menu. I also baked them for 15 minutes as suggested by a reader.

This was so easy and quick to make, I loved them! I added lemon zest to the cream cheese mix and really adds just that little more flavour. I also finished them in the oven under a low boiler just to give them a little candied crisp. Thanks for the great recipe.

These are so pretty! I only used half of the cream cheese mixture for 20 ounces of bread (yep, less mixture for more bread than called for). I rolled them tight and cut them in half diagonally before dipping them in butter. If you want to avoid having a plate with cinnamon sugar paste on it, sprinkle the cinnamon sugar on them instead of rolling. I had McCormick pre-mixed cinn-sugar and using that was great. I baked them for 15 minutes on parchment paper lined cookie sheets. (Parchment paper is my best friend in the kitchen). I didn't use the sour cream , just served them as is and got great compliments.

These were really good - but I made some changes to the recipe. Instead of bread, I used rectangular shapes wraps (this way I didn't have to cut of the crust or roll the bread flat. I used low fat cream cheese. Next time I will not ad the milk to the cream cheese mixture which made the mixture too thin. I followed other reviewers advice and didn't dip the blintzes into butter - Instead, I sprayed them with PAM and sprinkled them with sugar and cinnamon. They needed to bake longer than suggested.

Five stars for delicious. I just made these for a poker game tonight. Luckily, I had a backup plan, because these kind of flattened in the oven. Next time I'll freeze them first, as others suggested. They were still very good, and my family is having fun eating them as they are. I used half cream cheese and half mascarpone cheese, with a bit of powdered sugar added in. The hardest part was rolling out the bread!

This was so easy! They were just fine without the sour cream. I added a little confectioner's sugar to the cream cheese mixture to sweeten it just slightly. I doubled the vanilla as suggested by others. Instead of rolling the cheese blintzes in butter, I used a pastry brush to apply the butter. I sprinkled the cinnamon-sugar mixture on the tops, so I didn't have problems with the blintzes sticking to the pan.

We loved these. My whole family did. I make a dessert very similar to this with crescent rolls. I halved the recipe, but used full amount of vanilla and added 1/4 C sugar to cream cheese mixture because I like things very sweet. I did fine with rolling in butter and in cinn/sugar mix. Couldn't even tell I used just plain regular bread. Will make again!

Really, really good! I needed more of the sugar mixture then listed. I flattened the bread by rolling a can of soup over it and baked for 15 minutes to make the outside slightly crispy. This is an easy recipe for children who are learning to cook. I will make it again many times.

I was told to use 3 loaves of white bread and freeze the sugared blintzes on jelly roll plans and store them in the freezer once frozen in freezer zip bags.Then you can bake as many ias needed. Remember to place them seam side down. I doubled the butter you have listed and tripled the sugar so it covered 3 loaves of white bread. It is great for church coffee hours or brunches!

I'm in charge of six meals at a Youth Conference next month for 200 hungry teenagers, and I was looking for a breakfast item that would really wow the kids and the adults. So, I put together a "focus group" and they LOVED these things! I loved them because they both taste great and are super-easy to prepare. I added sugar to the cream cheese mix, and had some fruit topping (strawberries and blackberries) and whipped cream. The kids just went nuts. These are going to be a big hit next month. Thanks so much for this one!

This is a great recipe! For those who said it still tasted like white bread, you must not have rolled it out enough. Mine almost resembled a small flour tortilla after I rolled. I left them whole as well.
Delicious and so fast to get together! I would definitely make these again. This is the perfect dish to get your little ones to help with.

Yum!!!! These were easy to make and a tasty treat enjoyed by adults and toddlers alike. We didn’t use the sour cream for dipping, just ate them on their own. I would suggest following another reviewers suggestion of putting about half the cinnamon-sugar mixture in a small bowl to use first, then adding more as needed since the butter makes it start to clump up.
This was an easy recipe. It tasted like cheesecake and churros, and it was a balance of sweet and salty.I give it a 3.5 of 5 because it wasn't delicious but it was ok
They were okay, I'll probably make them again. I think they're missing something. I have no clue what, but there's just something not in the mix.
Okay, probably wouldn't make it again.

We had fun making this! I had assigned each family member to help out to make it easier. My daughter loves it but
I wasn't too thrilled with the overall taste...still have it a four though. I wished I had added sugar to the cream cheese or more sugar to the bread.
Absolutely wonderful recipe! I didn't cut the edges because I was lazy lol, but it still taste great. It was a huge hit with the family!

This is really good but the cream cheese mixture does need some white or powdered sugar to sweeten it up. Not sure how much I added. I think it was about half a cup but it might have been more. I was in a hurry so just sweetened to taste. The sweeter ones received many more complements and were gobbled up much faster. Definitely needed a lot more cinnamon sugar than the recipe called.
